sections.title: A) INVERSIONS
sections.subtitle: Adverbio negativo / restrictivo al principio → orden de pregunta

blocks.heading: ¿Qué es la inversión?
blocks.rule: Cuando una frase empieza por un adverbio negativo o restrictivo (never, rarely, little, not until, only when...), el sujeto y el auxiliar se invierten como en una pregunta. Es un registro formal y enfático: sube nota en Writing y en Speaking.

compare.label: Orden normal
compare.text: I have **never** seen such a heavy weight.

compare.label: Inversión
compare.text: **Never have I** seen such a heavy weight.

blocks.tip: Si la frase no tiene auxiliar (present / past simple), añade do / does / did: He seldom misses a session → Seldom **does he miss** a session.

blocks.heading: Never · Rarely · Seldom · Little
blocks.formula: Never / Rarely / Seldom / Little + AUX + SUJETO + verbo
blocks.rule: La inversión va justo después del adverbio (en la oración principal).
examples: **Never have I** lifted such a heavy weight on the bench press.
**Rarely do you** see someone with such perfect execution.
**Seldom does he** miss a training session.
**Little did I** know that those extra calories would make such a difference.
blocks.tip: Little casi siempre va con did + sujeto + know / realise / imagine / suspect (= no tenía ni idea).

blocks.heading: Hardly · Barely · Scarcely ... WHEN
blocks.formula: Hardly / Barely / Scarcely + HAD + SUJETO + participio + WHEN + past simple
blocks.rule: Una acción pasada ocurre justo después de otra (= apenas había... cuando...).
examples: **Hardly had I** finished my sets **when** the gym closed.
**Scarcely had we** left the house **when** it started to rain.

blocks.heading: No sooner ... THAN
blocks.formula: No sooner + HAD + SUJETO + participio + THAN + past simple
blocks.rule: Mismo significado que hardly, pero la partícula es THAN (no when).
examples: **No sooner had I** drunk the protein shake **than** it was time for the next meal.
**No sooner had they** got married **than** they started to argue.

wrong.bad: No sooner had I arrived when the phone rang.
wrong.good: No sooner had I arrived than the phone rang.

blocks.heading: Under no circumstances · In no way · On no account · At no time · Not only
blocks.formula: Expresión con NO / NOT + AUX + SUJETO + verbo
blocks.rule: La inversión va justo después de la expresión.
examples: **Under no circumstances should you** sacrifice technique to lift more weight.
**In no way will I** accept that kind of behaviour.
**On no account must this door** be left unlocked.
**At no time did my partner** doubt my ability to pass the exam.
**Not only did he** arrive late, **but he also** forgot his notes.

wrong.bad: At no time you can't use my car.
wrong.good: At no time can you use my car. (sin doble negación)

blocks.heading: Inversión en la SEGUNDA parte: Not until · Not since · Only when · Only if · Only after
blocks.formula: Not until / Only when ... + [oración normal] + AUX + SUJETO + verbo
blocks.rule: La primera parte se queda con orden normal; la inversión va en la oración PRINCIPAL (la segunda).
examples: **Not until** he apologised **did I** forgive him.
**Not since** I was a child **have I** eaten so much candy.
**Only when** you finish your homework **can you** play.
**Only if** it rains **will we** cancel the picnic.
**Only after** the meeting ended **did she** realise the mistake.

wrong.bad: Not until did Peter get home he realised...
wrong.good: Not until Peter got home did he realise...

blocks.heading: So + adjetivo · Such + be + sustantivo
blocks.rule: Para enfatizar una cualidad (so) o un sustantivo (such).

compare.label: So
compare.text: She was so supportive that... → **So supportive was she** that I managed to study every day.

compare.label: Such
compare.text: The demands of her job are such that... → **Such are the demands** of her job that she rarely takes a holiday.

blocks.heading: Inversión en condicionales (repaso Unidad 4)
blocks.rule: Se quita if y se invierte el auxiliar.

rows: Should + sujeto + inf, will / can + inf
Should you need more rice, let me know.
Were + sujeto + to + inf, would + inf
Were I to fail the test, I would take it again.
Had + sujeto + participio, would have + participio
Had we known, we would have organised a better dinner.

blocks.heading: Emphasis (Complete Advanced): cleft sentences
formulas: It + BE + [lo que enfatizas] + who / that + ...
blocks.rule: Partimos la frase para enfatizar una parte. Con What: si el verbo pide to-inf, usamos to (What I decided to do was to write...); si pide inf sin to, sin to (What you should do is arrange...). También All / The only thing / The last thing / The reason why... Con It eliges qué destacar.
examples: My brother wanted a new car. → **What** my brother wanted **was** a new car.
**What** you should do **is** arrange a dental appointment.
**All** I really wanted **was** to sleep all day.
**It was** Pete **who** had his bike repaired. (Pete, no Ben)
**It was** last weekend **that** Pete had his bike repaired.
**The last thing** I was expecting **was** to lose my job.

blocks.heading: Emphasis (Complete Advanced): fronting, do / did y reflexivos
blocks.rule: Fronting: empezar por lo que quieres destacar (lugar, comparativo, superlativo, so + adj); con lugar, a veces se invierte el verbo. Do / does / did + inf para enfatizar o llevar la contraria. Reflexivos (himself, herself...) para enfatizar quién lo hizo.
examples: **Next to me sat** an elderly man reading a newspaper.
**More important than anything else is** the need to look after the children.
**Best of all was** the sweet creamy dessert.
They **do** study enough, but the tests are too hard!
The manager **herself** wrote to us to apologise.

blocks.heading: Superioridad e inferioridad: cómo se forma
blocks.rule: 1 sílaba → -er · 2 sílabas acabadas en -y → -ier · 2+ sílabas → more + adj. Inferioridad: less + adj + than.

blocks.heading: Intensificadores de MÁS (mucho más...)
examples: This method is **far better** than the old one.
This exam was **a great deal harder** than the last one.
My sister is clever, but my brother is **even cleverer**.
It's more difficult **by a long way**.

wrong.bad: He is very taller than me.
wrong.good: He is much / far taller than me. (very no va con comparativos)

blocks.heading: Intensificadores de MENOS (un poco más...)
blocks.formula: a bit / a little / slightly + comparativo
examples: I'm feeling **a bit more tired** today.
Can you speak **a little louder**?
The temperature is **slightly lower** now.

blocks.heading: Igualdad: as ... as · the same ... as
examples: She is **just as talented as** her rival.
His car is **nowhere near as fast as** mine.
He is **twice as old as** me.
They have **the same car as** we do.

wrong.bad: He is twice older than me.
wrong.good: He is twice as old as me.

wrong.bad: She is not as athletic than she thinks.
wrong.good: She is not as athletic as she thinks.

blocks.heading: Superlativos e intensificadores
examples: She is **by far the most talented** artist here.
He is **easily the best** player on the team.
This is the worst movie **by a long way**.
He's **one of the best** singers I've ever heard.
It was **the simplest of** ideas.
We had **the worst weather imaginable**.

wrong.bad: This laptop is by far the better one.
wrong.good: This laptop is by far the best one.

blocks.heading: Doble comparativo: the more ..., the more ...
blocks.formula: THE + comparativo + sujeto + verbo, THE + comparativo + sujeto + verbo
blocks.rule: Causa y efecto: cuanto más..., más...
examples: **The more** I study, **the more** I learn.
**The harder** you work, **the luckier** you get.
**The less** I sleep, **the less** energy I have.
**The older** we grow, **the more** we know.

wrong.bad: The long I live here, the more I love it.
wrong.good: The longer I live here, the more I love it.

blocks.heading: more · most · less · fewer + sustantivo
blocks.rule: More / most + plural o incontable. Most of + determinante / pronombre (parte de un grupo concreto). Less + incontable. Fewer + plural.

compare.label: Less + incontable
compare.text: I'm getting **less money** now than in my last job.

compare.label: Fewer + plural
compare.text: There were **fewer people** than usual at the match.

examples: **Most sharks** are quite harmless.
**Most of our relatives** live in Canada.

rows: elder / eldest solo para familia y delante del sustantivo (my elder brother)

sections.title: C) GERUND vs TO-INFINITIVE
sections.subtitle: Qué forma va detrás de cada verbo, adjetivo o expresión

blocks.heading: Gerundio (-ing) como sujeto, complemento y tras preposiciones
blocks.rule: Como sujeto el gerundio va siempre en singular. Detrás de CUALQUIER preposición (in, of, about, without, before, after...) el verbo va en -ing.
examples: **Studying** English is very useful. (sujeto → singular)
My hobby **is reading**. (complemento)
**Instead of catching** the bus, I walked home.
Are you **interested in joining** our club?

blocks.heading: ¡TO como preposición! → + -ing
blocks.formula: look forward to / object to / be used to + V-ING
blocks.rule: En estas expresiones to es una preposición, no parte del infinitivo.

wrong.bad: I look forward to hear from you.
wrong.good: I look forward to hearing from you.

blocks.heading: Verbos + -ing
examples: He **denied stealing** the car.
I **suggest taking** the overnight train.
If I were you, I'd **consider spending** less time at work.

wrong.bad: I suggest to take the train.
wrong.good: I suggest taking the train / I suggest (that) we take the train.

blocks.heading: Phrasal verbs, conectores y expresiones fijas + -ing
blocks.rule: Expresiones fijas: can't stand, can't help, it's no use, it's not worth, there's no point (in), feel like, be / get used to.
examples: I **couldn't help laughing** at the joke.
It's **not worth arguing** with him.
I don't **feel like going** out tonight.

blocks.heading: To-infinitive: finalidad, adjetivos y sustantivos
examples: I went to England **to improve** my English.
I found it **impossible to sleep** because of the noise.
Everyone was **surprised to see** me.
She has the **ability to learn** quickly.
blocks.tip: Sustantivos + to inf: ability, attempt, chance, decision, desire, effort, intention, need, opportunity, permission, plan, refusal, right, tendency, way, willingness.

blocks.heading: Verbos + to-infinitive
examples: We can't **afford to go** on holiday.
I **pretended to understand** what she was saying.
blocks.tip: Would + like / love / hate / prefer → SIEMPRE to inf: I'd hate to get up early every day.

blocks.heading: Verbo + OBJETO + to-infinitive · y los que van SIN to
formulas: make / let / help + alguien + inf (sin to)
examples: My father **taught me to swim**.
You can't **force people to believe** something.
They **let the animals escape**.
She **helped me (to) revise**.
blocks.tip: Sin to también tras los modales (must, can, should...), had better y would rather.

blocks.heading: Verbos con -ing o to SIN cambio de significado
examples: I've just **started to learn / learning** to ski.

compare.label: like + to inf
compare.text: I like **to clean** my car every week. (lo hago porque es bueno, me centro en el resultado)

compare.label: like + -ing
compare.text: I like **cleaning** my car. (disfruto la actividad)

blocks.heading: Verbos que CAMBIAN de significado
blocks.rule: La regla general: -ing → algo anterior o en curso · to inf → algo posterior / un propósito.

rows: recordar algo que hiciste: I remember locking the door.
acordarse de hacer algo: Remember to lock the door.
olvidar algo que pasó: I'll never forget phoning her that night.
olvidarse de hacer algo: I forgot to phone my brother.
dejar de hacer algo: Stop worrying!
parar para hacer otra cosa: We stopped to look at the map.
probar algo como solución: Have you tried kicking it?
intentar algo difícil: I've been trying to repair it all morning.
seguir haciendo lo mismo: He went on walking.
pasar a hacer otra cosa: She went on to break the record.
implicar: It'll mean getting up at 5:00.
tener intención: I didn't mean to be rude.
arrepentirse de algo pasado: He regrets taking the day off.
lamentar decir (formal): I regret to inform you that...
ver parte de la acción: I saw the plane landing.
(inf sin to) ver la acción completa: I saw the plane land.

speaking.example: Not only does this approach save time, but it also provides a much better outcome in the long run.
speaking.translation: Este enfoque no solo ahorra tiempo, sino que también ofrece un resultado mucho mejor a largo plazo.

speaking.structure: Had it not been for [noun phrase], [consequence]...
speaking.example: Had it not been for the recent advances in technology, dealing with this problem would have been nearly impossible.
speaking.translation: Si no hubiera sido por los recientes avances tecnológicos, lidiar con este problema habría sido casi imposible.

speaking.example: Rarely do we see people taking this issue as seriously as they should nowadays.
speaking.translation: Rara vez vemos a la gente tomarse este problema tan en serio como debería hoy en día.

speaking.example: The more time people spend interacting through screens, the more isolated they seem to become.
speaking.translation: Cuanto más tiempo pasa la gente interactuando a través de pantallas, más aislada parece volverse.

speaking.structure: [Option A] is nowhere near as [adjective] as [Option B].
speaking.example: Reading about this online is nowhere near as effective as actually experiencing it first-hand.
speaking.translation: Leer sobre esto en internet no es ni de lejos tan efectivo como experimentarlo de primera mano.

speaking.structure: Taking everything into consideration, [option] is by far the most [adjective].
speaking.example: Taking everything into consideration, I'd say this option is by far the most practical one.
speaking.translation: Teniendo todo en cuenta, diría que esta opción es con diferencia la más práctica.

speaking.example: I can't help feeling that people are becoming increasingly disconnected from their surroundings.
speaking.translation: No puedo evitar sentir que la gente se está desconectando cada vez más de su entorno.

speaking.example: It's simply not worth spending time on options that won't make a real difference, so we ought to focus on...
speaking.translation: Simplemente no vale la pena dedicar tiempo a opciones que no marcarán una diferencia real, así que deberíamos centrarnos en...

speaking.structure: Despite [gerund]..., many people still struggle to [infinitive]...
speaking.example: Despite being fully aware of the consequences, the vast majority of people still struggle to change their daily habits.
speaking.translation: A pesar de ser plenamente conscientes de las consecuencias, a la gran mayoría de la gente todavía le cuesta cambiar sus hábitos diarios.
